beats.text: Before you train your next model, see how Cache Engineering for LLM Agents cuts 1.5x of memory overhead.
beats.visual_focus: A progress bar stuck at 99% with a red 'RE-COMPUTE' warning.

beats.text: The villain is the KV cache. Trimming history forces a full re-computation, like burning a library just to remove one outdated book.
beats.visual_focus: A massive stack of blocks collapsing as one is pulled from the bottom.

beats.text: Enter the AKV engine. It treats cache as a surgical tool, not a static block, allowing precise manipulation without re-prefilling.
beats.visual_focus: A surgical laser cutting a specific segment out of a data stream.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: Finally, a script that doesn't treat me like I'm five. The hook is solid because it addresses a real pain point—re-prefilling is the worst part of working with long-context LLMs. You didn't use any 'smart drawer' metaphors, and you actually explained the mechanism (pruning spans and shifting encodings) instead of just saying 'it makes it faster.' I'm actually interested in how you handle the position encoding shift without breaking the attention mechanism.
